nodes.title: Archiving a ticket silently archives its sub-issues, including NON-TERMINAL ones — and the parent-side check cannot detect it
nodes.description:
## BLUF

`issueArchive` **cascades to sub-issues.** Archiving 23 terminal tickets on 2026-09-08 also archived **KS-918 (Backlog)** and **KS-920 (In Progress)** — children of **KS-490**. Neither was in any target list. **In Progress is live work.**

**And the obvious verification cannot catch it:** once archived, the parent's `children` connection returns **nothing**. Asking the parent what it took with it reads clean.

Both were restored the same session. This ticket is about the mechanism, which is still live.

## Measured

```
child -> parent    KS-918.parent = KS-490      ✅ reveals the link
                   KS-920.parent = KS-490      ✅
parent -> children KS-490.children = 0         ❌ shows NOTHING
```

**The timestamps are what identified it as a cascade rather than a concurrent actor:**

```
KS-490  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-921  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-918  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
KS-920  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
```

Identical to the millisecond = one batch = one cause. **My own first diagnosis blamed a concurrent actor and was wrong; the timestamp disproved it.**

**Full accounting for the pass:** 33 intended + 2 collateral = 35 archived, measured 35. Only KS-490 had children, so the blast radius was bounded at exactly two.

## Why it went unnoticed until arithmetic caught it

The only reason anyone knows is the **census delta: −25 against an expected −23**. That is the shape most easily rationalised as a stale count. Every other signal looked clean:

* the archive calls all returned `success: true` — and they had, for the 23 asked;
* the parent-side `children` query returned **0**;
* no error, no warning, nothing in any response mentioning the children.

## The rule this produces

**Before archiving, query** `child → parent` **for the target's children and record the count. After, take a full paged census.**

```
expected delta = |targets| + |children found|
```

**If the delta is not exactly that, stop.** Asking the parent side for `children` is *the check that cannot fail* here — it reads zero both when there are none and when they have just been archived.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Make the children pre-check part of any archive procedure**, with the delta equation above as its pass condition.
- [ ] **2. Decide whether a cascade onto a NON-TERMINAL child should be refused outright.** Kam's standing ruling is that non-terminal work stays visible on the board; a cascade violates that silently.
- [ ] **3. Measure the historical population — see the sibling ticket** on the 95 pre-existing archived non-terminal tickets. This mechanism would produce exactly that.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the archive pass that hit it.
